Merville-Franceville, Normandy, France.launch_notes: Western end of the beach near the Orne estuary, next to the Kite-R Evolution school. Take Boulevard Wattier west to the wooden barrier that marks the kite zone. Parking at the barrier or on the access track is forbidden: park in the side streets and carry your gear along the dune path. Rig and launch at least 100 m away from the dune vegetation.
Merville-Franceville, Normandy, France.tide_notes: Works at all tides. Low tide gives flat water in the runnels (baïnes), good for beginners and freestyle, but it can mean a 30-minute walk back to the car. Waves break on the sandbanks on the ebb and at high tide. The beach is about 7 km long and up to 200 m wide, so some sand stays dry even at high tide.
Merville-Franceville, Normandy, France.hazards: Orne estuary and bird reserve to the west: riding is strictly prohibited in the last 300 m on the reserve side. Sandbanks and shallow water. Heavy crowding in summer, with dozens of kiters. The beach is shared with horse riders, hunters (Sept-Jan), shrimp and shellfish gatherers, swimmers and walkers. Cold water outside summer: in Feb 2020 two kiters were rescued and one had hypothermia.
Merville-Franceville, Normandy, France.rules: Described as the only Calvados beach where kitesurfing is allowed all year. In summer (July-August) kiting is limited to a marked zone on the western side. The ornithological reserve at the western end is closed to all riding. From 16 June to 30 Sept, horses are allowed only 05:00-09:00 and after 20:00, between the Orne estuary and the marked kite zone.
Merville-Franceville, Normandy, France.season: March-November. Riding is possible all year, with stricter rules in July-August.

Wissant, Pas-de-Calais, France.launch_notes: Windsurfers mostly use the left (west) part of the bay, kiters the right. At high tide everyone gathers in front of the reinforced seafront promenade, where the beach almost disappears. The south beach (Dune d'Aval) is reserved for water sports (kite, land yacht) and swimming is banned there. The beach is narrow, so take extra care when launching and landing. Gets crowded on good days.
Wissant, Pas-de-Calais, France.tide_notes: Big tidal range, so conditions vary a lot with the tide. Waves are best at high tide, but the rip and shorebreak are also strongest then and the beach is very narrow by the promenade. SW wind with a falling tide is the classic setup. Tidal current can reach several knots and pushes riders downwind.
Wissant, Pas-de-Calais, France.hazards: Strong tidal current (one guide cites up to 11 kn), so walking back upwind is common. Rip currents and shorebreak, worst at high tide. Narrow beach and seawall at high tide. Crowds on good days. Heavy shipping traffic in the Dover Strait offshore. Breakwater stakes at Sangatte on downwinders. Wartime ordnance occasionally found on the beach: a demining operation took place in Oct 2025.
Wissant, Pas-de-Calais, France.rules: South beach (Dune d'Aval) is reserved for water sports (kitesurf, land yacht) with swimming banned. Kite zoning is enforced more strictly in high season so beach users can share the space. Check the town hall's current beach order (arrêté).
Wissant, Pas-de-Calais, France.season: Usable all year. Strongest, most reliable winds roughly September to December; March to September also cited for kitesurfing.

Berck-sur-Mer, Pas-de-Calais, France.launch_notes: About 3 km of sandy beach from the Maritime Hospital (south) to Terminus beach (north). Main access is the Terminus car park (north, near the mussel beds) or the Saint-Nicolas car park. Northern beach is reached via Esplanade Parmentier past the Eole Club land-yacht base. In July-August, stay away from the swimming zones in front of the town centre.
Berck-sur-Mer, Pas-de-Calais, France.tide_notes: At low tide the sea goes out 2-3 km. Large tidal pools (baïnes) form, giving flat water for about 2.5 h around low tide, good for beginners. At high tide the water is 300-400 m from the seawall, with waves and shore break; intermediate+ in onshore wind. Currents are stronger on the falling tide. The rising tide fills in fast around the sandbanks and can cut people off.
Berck-sur-Mer, Pas-de-Calais, France.hazards: Bouchot mussel beds north of Berck, uncovered at low tide and marked with a yellow buoy. Waves and currents at high tide, especially on the falling tide. Fast rising tide around the sandbanks between Baie d'Authie and the main beach. Shore break at high tide in onshore wind. Summer crowds near the town centre. Baie d'Authie to the south is a confined area for experienced riders only.
Berck-sur-Mer, Pas-de-Calais, France.rules: Inside the 300 m coastal strip, the mayor sets the rules and speed is limited to 5 kn. In July-August, kiting is not allowed in the swimming zones in front of the town centre. Guide sources say kiting is banned in Baie d'Authie (Les Sternes) to protect a seal colony; windsurfing is allowed there.
Berck-sur-Mer, Pas-de-Calais, France.season: Year-round (windy coast); water is very cold in winter.

Hardelot, Pas-de-Calais, France.launch_notes: Launch on the beach in front of the Base de glisse Georges Pernoud (seafront, Hardelot-Plage). Changing rooms and showers at the base. Schools (e.g. Kitezone) and sand-yacht clubs share the beach, so give them space and keep clear of beach users when launching or landing. The north beach (towards the Becque estuary and dunes) is also used for watersports.
Hardelot, Pas-de-Calais, France.tide_notes: Large tidal range. At low tide the wide beach has baïnes (sandbar pools) with flat water over several km, the best conditions for beginners and freestyle. At high tide there is little beach, more waves and stronger current, so it gets more technical. Tidal current is moderate but real.
Hardelot, Pas-de-Calais, France.hazards: Tidal currents, especially around high tide. Shore break and reduced launch space at high tide. Busy in summer with swimmers, schools and sand yachts on the beach at low tide.
Hardelot, Pas-de-Calais, France.rules: In season, watersports are banned in the lifeguarded swimming zone at Plage Centrale (about 600 m long). Ride outside it and beyond the 300 m coastal strip rules. Schools run supervised zones in peak season. Check the current municipal order (Neufchâtel-Hardelot) for exact zone limits.
Hardelot, Pas-de-Calais, France.season: All year. Most consistent wind from October to March. Summer works but the beach is crowded.

Dunkerque Malo-les-Bains, France.launch_notes: Launch from the beach in front of the Station Nautique des Dunes de Flandre / base Licorne (Digue Nicolas II), next to the Parc du Vent, about 10 m from the beach. Home of the Dunkerque Flysurfing Club (DFC), which runs lessons and a kite simulator. The kite/sailing zone is the central beach along the Parc du Vent, between the Pavois and Terminus lifeguard posts. Stay out of the bathing areas at each end. The beach is shared with land yachts, cyclists and joggers.
Dunkerque Malo-les-Bains, France.tide_notes: Very large tidal range (about 4.7-5.5 m springs). Low to mid tide works best: the beach dries far out, giving lots of space, and riders stand in the shallows. Avoid high tide, when the beach shrinks; wait at least 1 h after high water. Falling tide is often quoted as best. Tidal current about 1-2 kn.
Dunkerque Malo-les-Bains, France.hazards: 3 rocky breakwaters offshore and 1 marked wreck east of the base. Offshore drift in S-SW winds. Moderate tidal current. Busy beach (land yachts, bikes, joggers, dogs), crowded at weekends. The port of Dunkerque lies to the west.
Dunkerque Malo-les-Bains, France.rules: Swimming is banned in the central kite/watersports zone along the Parc du Vent. The ends of the beach are bathing areas, with lifeguards in summer. From 1 July to 31 August, a prefectural order limits kiting to a zone 500 m west of the Terminus post, facing the Parc du Vent at the sailing base. The 'batteries' zone to the east (blockhouses, Leffrinckoucke dyke) is open all year.
Dunkerque Malo-les-Bains, France.season: Rideable all year (March-November most cited). April-August is best, with a peak in June.

Le Crotoy, Baie de Somme, France.launch_notes: Launch from the north end of Le Crotoy beach (plage nord / Plage du Marais, Chemin du Marais), where the official kite zone is. A ramp along the dike gives access. Parking near the beach, paid in some seasons. At high tide the launch strip is narrow: take turns when launching. Crowded on weekends and in summer.
Le Crotoy, Baie de Somme, France.tide_notes: Only rideable around high tide: about 2 h for small coefficients and up to 4 h for big ones. Best with coefficients 60-90. Below 60 the water does not come in far enough. Above 90 currents are strong and the beach floods quickly, leaving little room to launch. At low tide the sea goes out several hundred metres and you can end up stranded on the sand.
Le Crotoy, Baie de Somme, France.hazards: Strong estuary currents, especially when the tide turns; the falling tide pushes riders out to sea, mainly in side winds. Very shallow water with sandbanks and hidden obstacles. Muddy bottom in places. Fast-rising tide. Crowds on weekends. Birds and seals in the nearby reserve are easily disturbed.
Le Crotoy, Baie de Somme, France.rules: No board or kite sports in front of the built-up seafront, where currents are violent. Kitesurfing is banned in the Baie de Somme National Nature Reserve: do not go past the yellow buoys marking the reserve entrance. The town recommends these sports in the bay only for riders who already have training.

Cabourg, Normandy, France.tide_notes: Large tidal range. At low tide, big sandbanks shelter a shallow, flat lagoon-like area that suits beginners. At high tide there is shorebreak and the groynes are a hazard.
Cabourg, Normandy, France.hazards: Groynes (épis) along the beach, especially at high tide. Shorebreak at high tide. Shallow water and sandbanks at low tide. The Dives estuary and Port-Guillaume channel are next to Cap Cabourg. The beach gets crowded in summer.
Cabourg, Normandy, France.rules: The local school describes a ZRUK (Zone Réservée Uniquement au Kitesurf) open year-round, even in summer. Launch outside the supervised swimming zone and keep clear of surfers from the Cotentin Surf Club. The beach runs about 11 km north to Vauville, so there is room to spread out away from the village. No windsurf rental: the local club is surf-only, so bring your own gear.
Siouville, Cotentin, France.tide_notes: Shorebreak can be very violent at low tide. Waves are softer at high tide and hollower at low tide; mid-tide is generally best for waves.
Siouville, Cotentin, France.hazards: Powerful waves and heavy shorebreak, especially at low tide; experienced riders only. Rocky outcrop at the south end of the beach. Busy with surfers.
Siouville, Cotentin, France.rules: In season, all watersports (sailing, windsurf, surf, kitesurf, kayak...) are banned inside the supervised bathing area; lifeguard hours can shift with the tide, so check the flags and the municipal bylaw posted at the lifeguard post. Motorised watercraft banned on all beaches July 1 to Sept 15, 9am to 7pm.

Saint-Malo, Brittany, France.rules: Kitesurf is officially allowed at Plage du Sillon and Plage de Rochebonne (Saint-Malo city beach data). July–August restrictions reportedly apply 09:00–19:00. Check the current municipal order.
Saint-Malo, Brittany, France.season: Mostly September to May. Best wind March–May and in winter (Dec–Jan). Summer has NE thermals but more restrictions.

Bay side: 3 km sandy beach from Camping des Sables Blancs to the isthmus, for E/SE/NE winds. Parking at the isthmus. Schools use the bay side for beginners.
Penthièvre, Quiberon, Brittany, France.tide_notes: Bay side works mainly from mid-tide to low tide: shallow and standable, sheltered from swell and current. Ocean side tide behaviour for kiting is not documented. The surf break there is reported best around high tide.
Penthièvre, Quiberon, Brittany, France.hazards: Ocean side: exposed beach break with small to medium waves, and reefs are reported. Bay side: dike and oyster shells make it technical despite the flat water. Busy with schools in season.
Penthièvre, Quiberon, Brittany, France.rules: Ocean side: the north zone (accesses 10-11) is a take-off/landing-only zone. Bay side: kite and other air-towed sports banned from 29 May to 11 September in front of the beach at the southern end of Camping de Penthièvre (reported dates; check the current municipal order).
Penthièvre, Quiberon, Brittany, France.season: Year-round. Strongest and most reliable west winds are Oct-Mar, best Jan-Mar, for experienced riders. Lighter summer winds (weakest in July) suit the bay side. Schools operate Mar-Nov.

At low tide the beach is wide with sandbanks, but the 'Méchants' rocks are exposed on the NW of Pors Carn. At Pors Carn, rising tide is preferred because of the many rocks; some rocks midway along the beach are covered at high tide.
La Torche, Brittany, France.hazards: Powerful waves, often mast-high or more. Strong rip current running out along the point, plus baïnes and strong lateral currents. The 'Méchants' reef and its currents must be avoided. Rocky outcrop splitting the bay. The right side is for experienced wave riders only. Heavy crowds of bathers and surfers in summer.

Natura 2000 site: keep inside the marked boundaries.
La Torche, Brittany, France.season: September to May; spring peak (March-May, May best); frequent strong WSW winds November-March.

Lacanau, Gironde, France.hazards: Baïnes (bowls between sandbars) produce strong seaward rip currents, especially on the falling tide. Powerful shore break. Sandbars that keep moving. Some alios (hard sandstone) outcrops can damage fins. Crowded with swimmers and surfers in summer.
Lacanau, Gironde, France.rules: In summer during the day, only Plage Sud is open to kiting. Stay out of the lifeguarded swimming zones and keep downwind of them. On Lac de Lacanau, kitesurfing is only allowed on either side of the channel leading to Talaris marina (separate spot). Check the current municipal and prefecture orders on site.
Lacanau, Gironde, France.season: All year; autumn (September–November) for steady wind and swell; summer for the thermal NW breeze, with restrictions.

Alternative: Plage des Culs-Nus in the north, next to Les Estagnots (Seignosse), which is the recommended spot in summer. Stay clear of swimmers, walkers and the many surf schools. Windsurf beginners use Lac d'Hossegor instead (Plage du Rey sailing school, Plage des Chênes-Lièges, Plage Blanche, Plage du Parc).

Hours are 12:30–18:30, except 11:00–19:00 from 4 Jul to 30 Aug. No animals on the beach.
Hossegor, Landes, France.season: Autumn to spring (Sep–May) for Plage Sud outside supervised hours, with strong W–NW fronts in winter. In summer, N–NW afternoon thermals are better used at Les Estagnots.

Cross-onshore. Within the best range given by boards.co.uk.
Onshore-ish. Usable at Le Phare. SW is reported as the best direction for the main La Tranche beach.
Onshore at Le Phare. Best direction for the main town beach (sailing school).
Given as the southern limit of the usable onshore range at Le Phare.
Usable, but northerly components cause an inshore wind shadow (gusty near the beach), especially at the main beach.
Northern limit of the usable range. Wind shadow inshore, gusty.
Rare. Sideshore-to-side-off at Le Phare, moderate and gusty.
Offshore.
Offshore.

La Tranche-sur-Mer, Vendée, France.launch_notes: Summer kite zone at Plage du Phare is in front of the ruined bunker to the west. Beyond it, yellow buoys mark shallows on the point. Free parking at Impasse de la Youte, with beach accesses 146/147. Windsurf beginners usually use the main La Tranche beach (sailing school, sandy bottom, rescue boats). Le Phare is for experienced riders.
La Tranche-sur-Mer, Vendée, France.tide_notes: Le Phare works best from mid-tide to high water, when the beach gets narrow. Near low tide the rocky shelf is exposed or shallow. At high tide with big coefficients, shorebreak is powerful and stronger currents make entry and exit hazardous. The main La Tranche beach works at any tide.
La Tranche-sur-Mer, Vendée, France.hazards: Rocky shelf under the break and rocks around the point (marked by yellow buoys). Shorebreak and strong currents at high tide, plus baïnes. Lobster-pot lines and large jellyfish. With swell, the spot becomes a technically demanding wave spot.
La Tranche-sur-Mer, Vendée, France.rules: Kitesurf May–Sept: allowed only at Plage du Phare (designated zone). Off-season: allowed everywhere except Plage de la Belle Henriette (nature reserve). Lifeguards on Plage du Phare in summer; keep clear of the bathing area.
La Tranche-sur-Mer, Vendée, France.season: May–September (thermal NW sea breeze, mid-May to end of August); autumn and winter for frontal SW–NW winds

Leucate La Franqui, France.name: Leucate La Franqui (Les Coussoules)

wind.note: Tramontane veering north is side-shore. Flat to choppy water.
Tramontane, the reference wind. It blows cross-offshore and gusty, often 25-40+ kn. Flat water and chop for bump & jump, freeride and freestyle. For experienced riders only.
The Tramontane gets more offshore and gusty here. Drift risk out to sea.
Straight offshore.
Side-onshore.
Onshore. Waves build and tend to dump on the beach.
Marin: humid onshore wind, mostly in summer. Gives surfable waves and a dumping shore break.
Side-onshore. Waves tend to dump on the beach.

Leucate La Franqui, France.launch_notes: Park next to Camping des Coussoules / Domaine La Franqui. Walk about 300 m along the beach to the kite zone in front of the (old) lifeguard tower. The launch area is secured by the local association (KSL) and shared by independent riders and the many schools. The northern part toward Le Goulet is for windsurfers only.
Leucate La Franqui, France.tide_notes: Mediterranean: tide is negligible and the spot does not depend on it.
Leucate La Franqui, France.hazards: Cross-offshore Tramontane is strong and gusty and can push you out to sea. If you break gear or the wind drops, you drift offshore. When the wind turns onshore, a dumping shore break forms. The beach gets busy with schools and events such as the Mondial du Vent in April. In the nearby lagoon, oyster beds are marked by wooden posts.
Leucate La Franqui, France.rules: During the supervised summer season the first 300 m from shore is the bathing band. Kites and windsurfs must cross it only through the marked nautical channel and ride beyond it. Local beach marking is set by municipal orders (e.g. arrêté n°32-2010 on beach marking). Le Goulet area is reserved for windsurf.
Leucate La Franqui, France.season: March-April and July-October (Tramontane most consistent in spring); rideable year-round

Leucate Plage, France.name: Leucate Plage (Les Pilotis / Le Mouret)

wind.note: Tramontane, the dominant local wind (often 300+ days/yr), blows offshore here: flat water and fast runs per the tourist office, but it is strong and gusty and pushes riders out to sea. Experienced riders only, with rescue cover.
Offshore or cross-offshore with Tramontane gusts.
Offshore.
Marin, onshore: regular moderate thermal wind in summer, waves in the off-season. Suits bump & jump.
Side-shore. Lifts waves on this stretch of coast.
Onshore, sea state builds.

Leucate Plage, France.launch_notes: Sandy sea beach at Les Pilotis / Le Mouret, between Leucate Plage and the oyster centre. Beach clubs on site. Motorhome parking at Aire de Mouret. Le Mouret is a protected natural beach: respect bathers and keep the beach clear.
Leucate Plage, France.tide_notes: Mediterranean: tide is negligible. Water level changes with wind (storm surge in Marin, lower water in Tramontane).
Leucate Plage, France.hazards: Offshore Tramontane: strong gusts and drift out to sea. Shore break and waves in onshore wind. Water stays shallow for a short distance from shore. Bathers in summer.
Leucate Plage, France.season: Spring and autumn for the strongest wind; summer for the thermal Marin (SE).

Gruissan, Aude, France.name: Gruissan

wind.note: Tramontane, the dominant wind, Apr-Oct in 3-6 day spells. Offshore to side-offshore: flat, glassy water and long speed runs. Gusty near the Chalets buildings, steadier past the dike towards Vieille Nouvelle. Experienced riders only.
Tramontane can swing to straight offshore. Gusty, high drift risk.
Straight offshore at a SE-facing beach (estimated from the coast orientation).
Cross-shore, lets you get back to the beach on either tack.
Cross-shore, lets you get back to the beach on either tack.
Marin: onshore, brings waves, good for freeride.

Gruissan, Aude, France.launch_notes: Two sea launches. Plage des Chalets (Pôle Mer / Akila school at the beach entrance, Défi Wind venue). La Vieille Nouvelle, south of the Chalets past the dike: the reference Tramontane spot, runs of 10+ km towards Port-la-Nouvelle, wind stronger and steadier there. Driving onto the Vieille Nouvelle beach is banned (reported €1,500 fine): access on foot from the Chalets or via the canal. Lagoon options: Étang de Mateille, La Nautique, Grazel.
Gruissan, Aude, France.hazards: Offshore Tramontane: risk of drifting out to sea, and the wind is gusty and turbulent at the Chalets because of the buildings. Getting overpowered on strong days (wind can gain 10+ kn between Gruissan and Port-la-Nouvelle). Vieille Nouvelle has no lifeguards. Waves in Marin. At La Nautique lagoon: stone blocks and broken tiles on the bottom.
Gruissan, Aude, France.rules: In summer, launching from the Plage des Chalets is banned because of the swimming zone: launch from the marked channels and go beyond the 300 m strip. No vehicles on the Vieille Nouvelle beach.
Gruissan, Aude, France.season: April to October (Tramontane season). Wind more than 300 days a year.

Port-la-Nouvelle, Aude, France.name: Port-la-Nouvelle – Plage Sud

wind.note: Marin: onshore to cross-onshore, builds a medium to powerful beach break at Plage Sud. Waves are cleaner north of the breakwaters, but you have to cross the harbour channel to get there.
Marin variant, onshore with beach break.
Occasional NE thermal between Gruissan and La Franqui, usually around 15 kn.
Tramontane: offshore here, flat water but it pushes you out to sea. Guides say experienced riders only. Unsafe without rescue; ride the Etang de La Palme instead (onshore there).
Offshore at the sea beach.

Port-la-Nouvelle, Aude, France.launch_notes: Plage Sud, south of the harbour jetties. Sandy beach with parking. Usually much less crowded than nearby spots (Leucate, Gruissan).
Port-la-Nouvelle, Aude, France.tide_notes: Mediterranean, tidal range negligible. Conditions depend on wind and swell, not tide.
Port-la-Nouvelle, Aude, France.hazards: Medium to powerful shore break in Marin. Harbour channel and breakwaters at the north end of the beach, with commercial port traffic. Offshore Tramontane (NW) carries riders out to sea.

Almanarre, Hyères, France.name: L'Almanarre

wind.note: Mistral blows cross-onshore from the right, often Force 6-9. It is usually a little weaker here than further south. Gusty, with choppy water and closing-out waves that suit jumping more than wave riding.
Mistral sector. Cross-onshore, powerful and gusty, with waves breaking on a small reef upwind.
Onshore to cross-onshore. A reference direction, with choppy water and waves.
Libeccio, up to about 20 kn. A reference direction, cross-onshore from the left.
Northerly Mistral turns side-shore to side-off from the right, so it gets gustier near the beach.
Offshore for this west-facing beach. Some guides describe flat, glassy water for experienced riders who can go upwind, but drifting out to sea is a real risk. Not suitable for most riders.
Some guides list it as usable, but it is side-off on a west-facing beach. Experienced riders only.

Almanarre, Hyères, France.launch_notes: Main kite zone: Route du Sel, between beach accesses 16 and 21. In summer it is marked by wooden posts with FFVL flags. The beach is narrow (about 150 m) with the road right behind it, so take off and land carefully and do not rig on the road. The water gets deep quickly. Quieter alternatives on the same beach: La Madrague (shallower, smaller waves) and behind Camping International, both with buoyed kite zones in summer. A welcome point with a beach marshal runs in July and August.
Almanarre, Hyères, France.tide_notes: Mediterranean, almost no tide; it does not affect sessions.
Almanarre, Hyères, France.hazards: Narrow beach with a road just behind, so launching and landing are risky. Strong, gusty Mistral. The water gets deep quickly. Waves close out in Mistral. There are rocks to the right of the launch. Crowded on the water and in the car parks when the wind is good, and cars at the car parks get broken into.
Almanarre, Hyères, France.rules: Kitesurfing is allowed only in the designated zones (Almanarre between accesses 16 and 21, plus two other designated zones). Riding is forbidden inside the 300 m strip from shore except in the marked channels, which are in place from April to October. Stricter rules apply from 15 June to 15 September, when the Route du Sel is open and summer zones are buoyed. A beach marshal and municipal police on jet-ski patrol in summer and can fine riders who break the rules.
Almanarre, Hyères, France.season: October to April for the most wind (Mistral). Summer works too, but with more restrictions and crowds.

Beauduc, Camargue, France.name: Beauduc

wind.note: Mistral is the reference wind here: cross-shore, flat to slightly choppy water, often strong and not too gusty over the flat salt marshes. Guides say about 15 kn is ideal, but winter Mistral can reach 60 kn.
Mistral/Tramontane sector, cross-shore. Listed as a main direction on kiteforum. Can build small waves when strong.
Mistral/Tramontane, cross-shore, regularly 25-30 kn. The right-hand side of the beach is preferred by windsurfers in side-shore Mistral.
Listed among the good directions. The U-shaped bay keeps it rideable.
Reliable summer thermal, side-shore to side-on, good for learning. The beach can flood in strong SW.
Side-on, rideable. Recommended for learners together with SW.
Sources disagree: one guide calls SE offshore and dangerous (schools move north), another lists it as a usable wind. Check on site.
Straight easterly is described as the only fully offshore wind. Do not ride.

Beauduc, Camargue, France.launch_notes: Kites launch and land on the right-hand part of the beach (Plage de la Comtesse), which is set aside for kites and other sail sports. Kitesurfers use the left side in onshore winds, where the water is deeper. Shallow water for about 100 m. Huge sand area with no walk from parking. No water, toilets or shops except a small snack bar in summer. Take your waste back to town.
Beauduc, Camargue, France.tide_notes: Mediterranean, so tide is negligible. Strong SW wind and storm surge can flood the low-lying beach and the parking area.
Beauduc, Camargue, France.hazards: Weever fish (vives) buried in the sand, stings can go through soft booties. Very remote, with weak or no phone signal, so rescue is slow; carry a first-aid kit. Cars can sink in soft sand. Beach floods in strong SW. Offshore drift in E/SE winds. Crowded in summer. Mosquitoes.
Beauduc, Camargue, France.rules: Protected natural site (communes of Arles and Saintes-Maries). Arles municipal order of 27/03/2014 and prefectoral order of 30/09/2013: Plage de la Comtesse is reserved for kites and sail sports, and the southern part for swimming and fishing. Motor vehicles and land sail sports are banned on the public maritime land of the point from 1 April to 30 September. Camping banned since 2018, dunes off-limits. Track limited to vehicles about 2.0-2.1 m wide; quads, motorbikes and campervans banned.
Beauduc, Camargue, France.season: Year-round. Best April-October, with June-July the peak (thermals and moderate Mistral). Strong Mistral in winter.

Saint-Cyprien, Pyrénées-Orientales, Fran.name: Saint-Cyprien – Plage Nord

wind.note: Tramontane, the dominant local wind. It blows offshore here because the beach faces east, and it is often strong and gusty.
Offshore on an east-facing beach.
Side-shore to side-off along a north-south coastline. Likely gusty.
Marin, the onshore sea wind. Sources do not rate it as best or ok, so this rating is inferred from the beach orientation.

Saint-Cyprien, Pyrénées-Orientales, Fran.launch_notes: Launch from Plage Nord (Boulevard Desnoyer). It has one marked channel for windsurfing and a separate one for kitesurfing, so use the kite channel to get in and out. The town and the local association have put signs across the whole practice area. Two water-sports clubs, including CBCM Boarder Club at 75 Bd Desnoyer, give lessons and rent gear.
Saint-Cyprien, Pyrénées-Orientales, Fran.tide_notes: Mediterranean with very little tide. Tide has almost no effect on sessions.
Saint-Cyprien, Pyrénées-Orientales, Fran.hazards: Swimmers and lifeguard zones on the beach in summer. Strong, gusty tramontane blows offshore. The harbour is to the south of Plage Nord.
Saint-Cyprien, Pyrénées-Orientales, Fran.rules: Use the marked kite and windsurf channels. Lifeguard station no. 1 is on the beach. Dogs are not allowed on the beach. Parking is paid in July and August. I did not find the text of the municipal order.

Carro, Martigues, France.name: Carro

wind.note: Cross-shore from the left; biggest waves (1.5-3 m) but choppy. Reference wave-riding direction.
S/SE winds give the classic wave sessions.
Reported as working with swell.
Usable, but easterlies can blow out the waves.
Listed as a working direction; often lighter.
Mistral: cross-off from the right, clean reef-break waves, but there is a risk of being blown offshore. Experts only, and only if you can go upwind well.
Northerly Mistral is offshore and flattens the waves; guides suggest La Cabane, about 500 m west, instead.

Carro, Martigues, France.launch_notes: No real beach at the wave spot: you launch from a rocky shelf on slippery slabs near Pointe de Carro. Large car parks on Rue des Ragues on the way out to the point. Advanced riders only. Kiting is described as tricky or impractical because of the rocky launch and landing. Equipment theft is reported, so do not leave gear unattended.
Carro, Martigues, France.hazards: Rocky reef and abrasive bottom with underwater holes, mussel-covered rocks and sea urchins, strong currents, heavy shore break, waves up to about 2 m, a dike/jetty near the port, and a risk of drifting offshore in Mistral.
Carro, Martigues, France.season: Year-round; often windy (Mistral and SE storms), and autumn to spring brings the most wave days.

Tarifa Los Lances, Spain.name: Tarifa Los Lances

wind.note: Levante: strong, warm, gusty; side-off from the left at Los Lances. Most popular kite wind here, but drift risk out to sea; rescue boat service operates in Levante. Medium/small kites.
Poniente: steady, cooler, side-on/onshore from the right. Wide beach makes it easy to find space. Medium/large kites.

Tarifa Los Lances, Spain.launch_notes: 7+ km sandy beach with many access points and car parks along the beach road (Rio Jara, Football Field, Los Carriles, others near town). Rio Jara area is the main launch in Levante. In summer use only the marked kite zones; respect school and swimmer zones. Area north of the kite zone up to La Peña is reserved for windsurfing. Arrive early in high season.
Tarifa Los Lances, Spain.hazards: Levante is gusty and side-off, with drift risk out to sea. Shore break, especially with swell. Crowded, sometimes hectic, mostly in Levante. Wind is stronger near Tarifa town. Protected lagoon (La Charca) halfway along the beach: riding inside the staked area is forbidden.
Tarifa Los Lances, Spain.rules: Marked zones (yellow buoys) separate swimmers, kite schools and freeriders in summer; strictly enforced in summer, more relaxed in winter. Kiting in the protected lagoon is forbidden and can be fined.

Tarifa Valdevaqueros, Spain.name: Tarifa Valdevaqueros

wind.note: Levante is the reference wind here, side-offshore, often strong and gusty, so small to medium kites. Outside summer it is called the safest Tarifa spot in Levante because Punta Paloma limits the risk of drifting out to sea.
Levante turning more offshore. Risk of drifting out. 'If no-one else is out in Levante, don't even think about it.'
Poniente: the easiest wind, lighter, needs bigger kites. Los Lances is usually preferred in Poniente because it has more space. Summer thermal effect around midday on warm days.
Poniente/thermal side-onshore. Usable with large kites (12-15 m) on light days.

Tarifa Valdevaqueros, Spain.launch_notes: The summer kite zone is the southern part of the beach, in front of Bibo bar. The northern part, up to the dunes, is for windsurfers. Respect the marked kite, windsurf and swimmer zones (yellow buoys). Access is by exits from the N-340. Parking fills up quickly in summer.
Tarifa Valdevaqueros, Spain.tide_notes: At high tide a small lagoon fills at the river mouth and gives flat water for tricks. No other tide guidance was found in the sources.
Tarifa Valdevaqueros, Spain.hazards: Rocks on the beach and underwater rocks at the southern end, inside the summer kite zone. The zone is narrow and very crowded in summer. Levante is side-offshore and can carry riders out to sea. Gusty, very strong Levante days.
Tarifa Valdevaqueros, Spain.rules: Kite and windsurf zones are strictly enforced in summer when the beaches are crowded. Schools give this period as about 15 June to 15 September. Swimmer areas are marked by yellow buoys. Rules are more relaxed in winter.
Tarifa Valdevaqueros, Spain.season: All year. Spring and autumn are best for Levante and space. Summer has reliable thermals but restricted, crowded zones.

El Médano, Tenerife, Spain.name: El Médano – Playa Sur (Leocadio Machado)

wind.note: Reference trade wind (alisios), side/cross-onshore from the left. Funnelled and strengthened by the island relief. Typically 16-25 kn, strongest in Jul-Aug.
Prevailing direction in the stats (73-89°). Cross-onshore from the left.
Usable trade-wind variant. Gusty close to the shore, especially near the northern jetty.
The tourist board lists N and NE as the good directions, mainly in summer. It turns more side-shore, so expect gusts near the beach.
Onshore-leaning. Usable, more chop.
Offshore given the SE-facing beach (inferred from orientation, not stated in guides).
Offshore given the SE-facing beach (inferred from orientation).
Offshore given the SE-facing beach (inferred from orientation).

El Médano, Tenerife, Spain.launch_notes: Sandy beach that shelves slowly into deep water. A dedicated kite set-up zone is on the beach. Kiters use the southern part of the bay, downwind of the windsurfers, and launch/land downwind (leeward) of the bunker. Windsurfers stay further upwind (north). Schools, rentals and gear storage containers are on the seafront.
El Médano, Tenerife, Spain.tide_notes: Guides say it works at any tide. Watch out at low tide for exposed rocks just off and to the right of the launch, and around El Cabezo (the 'Godzilla' rock).
El Médano, Tenerife, Spain.hazards: Rocky shore downwind with very few places to land, so don't drift past the bay. Gusty wind close inshore. Shore break, waves 1-2 m. Strong currents and swell outside the bay, where riding is not advised. Current near the northern jetty. Sand and volcanic reef bottom, with sea urchins on the rocky slabs at El Cabezo. The spot gets crowded with windsurfers, kiters and schools. Lifeguards on duty.
El Médano, Tenerife, Spain.rules: Kite and windsurf zones are separate: kites in the south of the bay, windsurfers upwind. Montaña Roja (south end) is a Special Nature Reserve. Its specific kite restrictions were not confirmed.
El Médano, Tenerife, Spain.season: All year round thanks to the trade winds. Strongest Jun-Sep, especially Jul-Aug.

Pozo Izquierdo, Gran Canaria, Spain.name: Pozo Izquierdo

wind.note: Reference trade wind (alisio). Cross-onshore from the left. Funnelled by the island's relief, it is often very strong in summer (sometimes up to ~50 kn). Makes downwind wave riding technical.
Northerly variant of the trade wind; usable but less established than NE.
Usable trade wind, more onshore.
Winter trade wind shifts east: lighter, less funnelled at Pozo. Southern spots (Bahía Feliz, Playa del Águila) are often better then.
Offshore.

Pozo Izquierdo, Gran Canaria, Spain.launch_notes: Launch from the main beach, El Arenal, in front of the Centro Internacional de Windsurfing (car parks, shops, schools). The beach is unofficially reserved for windsurfers. Entry and exit over loose dark lava boulders, so booties are recommended. Swimmers belong in the sheltered Playa del Ribanzo cove, behind the jetties.
Pozo Izquierdo, Gran Canaria, Spain.tide_notes: At high tide the wave breaks directly on the rocky shore, which makes entry and exit tricky and risks gear damage. At low tide the water is often choppy and messier without swell. With an Atlantic swell the waves can get big.
Pozo Izquierdo, Gran Canaria, Spain.hazards: Loose lava boulders at the water's edge; shorebreak on rocks at high tide; very strong, gusty wind; big waves when swell meets wind. Expert spot. Wave riders and PWA events crowd the water in summer. Don't swim beyond the Ribanzo jetties: risk of being hit by a windsurfer.
Pozo Izquierdo, Gran Canaria, Spain.rules: Kitesurfing is reported as prohibited in Pozo Izquierdo bay; kiters use Salinas de Tenefé (Pozo south) instead. Venue of the PWA Windsurf World Cup (usually July–August), when the water is reserved for the event.
Pozo Izquierdo, Gran Canaria, Spain.season: Year-round, best May–September (strongest trade winds June–August); calmer, more easterly winds in winter.

Guincho, Portugal.name: Guincho

wind.note: Reference direction: the summer Nortada blows side-shore and is strengthened by a thermal effect from the Sintra hills. Usually 15-25 kn, sometimes 35-40 kn, and often gusty.
Side-shore to slightly cross-on from the right. This is the typical summer thermal direction.
Cross-onshore from the right. Rideable, but the sea gets rougher with swell.
Cross-onshore. Expect a gusty thermal that swings between WNW and NW.
Listed as a working direction in spot guides. It is onshore, so expect heavy waves and shorebreak.
On very hot days the wind veers cross-offshore NNE. It is very gusty.
Offshore. When it gets too hot the wind can turn NE/E and then die completely.
Offshore.

Guincho, Portugal.launch_notes: Wide sandy beach about 100 m deep with plenty of space. Launch in the middle of the beach, north or south of the central rocks. You can exit at either end. Keep to the northern side so you stay out of the surfers' way.
Guincho, Portugal.tide_notes: Mid-low to mid-high tide is best: waves break on the outside and leave flat planing water between sets. At high tide the shorebreak and waves can be very powerful.
Guincho, Portugal.hazards: Rocks at both ends and in the middle of the beach, on the sand and in the water. Strong currents and rip currents: one narrow rip in the middle of the beach running out at an angle, another next to the rocks. Heavy swell and shorebreak. Gusty wind. Busy with surfers. Suited to intermediate and expert riders.

Lagoa de Óbidos, Portugal.name: Lagoa de Óbidos

wind.note: Summer Nortada thermal, usually 15-20 kn, starts around 1 pm; hills funnel it down the lagoon, venturi effect strengthens it. Steady and reliable.
Nortada variant, funnelled down the lagoon; described as cross-shore.
Works; cross-onshore at Foz do Arelho.
Cross-shore at Foz do Arelho; one of its reference directions.
Land wind, mostly off-season; gusty.
Rideable on the lagoon but gusty; strengthened by nearby hills.

Lagoa de Óbidos, Portugal.launch_notes: Most riders launch near Foz do Arelho on the lagoon side. In summer, when kiting is banned in the estuary and northern lagoon, use the windsurf school area ('Este') or Praia do Bom Sucesso / Vau on the far bank. North end near Bom Sucesso: sandy beach, flat water, beginners. Inside lagoon: pebble beach. Respect the school/teaching zone and ride upwind of it.
Lagoa de Óbidos, Portugal.tide_notes: Tidal lagoon; mid to high tide preferred. Low tide exposes sandbanks: long fins catch, you may end up walking, and the top of the lagoon is unusable. Inside the lagoon it works on both tides but gets choppy with strong current at high tide. At Foz do Arelho, high tide brings a heavy shore break on the ocean side.
Lagoa de Óbidos, Portugal.hazards: Strong currents at the estuary mouth. Sandbars and very shallow water at low tide. Sea urchins and seaweed inside the lagoon (wear booties). Gusty winds from S and E. Ocean-side shore break at Foz do Arelho can be big and powerful in swell. Many swimmers in summer.
Lagoa de Óbidos, Portugal.rules: Seasonal ban: kiting prohibited in the estuary and northern lagoon in summer (TheKiteSpot gives 15 Jun-15 Sep for the top of the lagoon). Kiting not officially allowed at Foz do Arelho in high summer due to swimmers. Designated kite/wingfoil zones and a teaching zone exist.
Lagoa de Óbidos, Portugal.season: April to October; June to September for the most reliable Nortada.

Esposende, Portugal.name: Esposende – Cávado River / Ofir

wind.note: Nortada, the summer north wind boosted by afternoon thermals. Flat water in the river. Reported as weaker than at Viana do Castelo.
Summer thermal flow, mostly N to NW according to the guides.
Common summer direction (around 292-306° in monthly statistics). Usable in the river and on the sea side.

Esposende, Portugal.launch_notes: Main launch: the sand beach at the tip of the Ofir spit, inside the nature reserve on the south bank of the Cávado across from the town. Kite schools run boat transfers from Esposende. By land it is a long walk from the beach parking, up to an hour. You can also launch from the town side. The river gets crowded with beginners, so give school lessons room.
Esposende, Portugal.tide_notes: Tidal estuary. At low tide the flat-water area shrinks to a small shallow zone. At high tide the current can be strong and there is shore break on the sea side.
Esposende, Portugal.hazards: Strong tidal current at certain times of the high tide. Shore break at high tide. Waves on the sea side, medium between Ofir's two breakwaters and bigger with swell. The river spot is crowded with beginners. Boat traffic from the school shuttles.
Esposende, Portugal.rules: A marked kite zone is in place during the summer months. The narrow road from the town to the beach closes seasonally. Check with the local schools for current zoning.
Esposende, Portugal.season: April to October. Best from May or June to September, when the thermal Nortada blows.

Lake Garda Torbole, Italy.name: Torbole (Conca d'Oro), Lake Garda

wind.note: Ora: thermal southerly, from roughly 12-13h until late afternoon on sunny days, March-October. Typically 20-25 kn on good days, with up to 1 m of chop. It strengthens towards the north of the lake. Clouds or low pressure weaken it.
Ora sector, side-on to onshore along the north shore. Main direction for slalom, freeride and the One Hour Classic crossings to Casa della Trota.
Pelèr: strong northerly from dawn to mid-morning (about 7-11h, varies by season), strongest in the north (Torbole, Malcesine). Side-off near the beach, so the wind is gusty close to shore.
Pelèr sector, side-off to offshore from the beach. Experienced riders only, and the morning kite windows apply.

Lake Garda Torbole, Italy.launch_notes: Windsurf and wing launch from Conca d'Oro / Molo Paradiso or from the Circolo Surf Torbole beach. There is a large lawn to rig on, a bar and parking nearby. The beach is pebbly, with a rubber mat to protect gear. Wind is steadier 50-70 m out. To avoid crowds, go upwind towards the tunnel or cross to Casa della Trota. Kitesurf: shore launches are not allowed. You must use an official boat lift service (Surf Segnana Torbole, Sailing Du Lac Riva) and stay at least 200 m from shore.
Lake Garda Torbole, Italy.hazards: Very crowded water in front of Conca d'Oro in summer. Public ferries (stay 200 m away). Regattas and race courses. Pebble beach. Gusty, side-off wind near shore in Pelèr. Ora chop up to about 1 m.
Lake Garda Torbole, Italy.rules: Garda Trentino kite rules: official lift service only, at least 200 m from shore and from public transport boats, no kiting during regattas, good weather only, wind up to 16 m/s. 1 Mar-9 Oct: kiting allowed from sunrise to 10:30 and from 16:30 to sunset, banned at midday, and only in designated areas after 18:00. 10 Oct-28 Feb: allowed from sunrise to sunset everywhere in Garda Trentino.
Lake Garda Torbole, Italy.season: March-October for the Ora. Spring (April-June) has better wind and fewer crowds. Summer is the most crowded.

Lo Stagnone, Marsala, Sicily, Italy.name: Lo Stagnone

wind.note: Maestrale/Mistral, the main summer direction, often thermally boosted, about 16-20 kn from spring to autumn. Flat water behind the salt-pan walls and Isola Lunga.
Part of the Maestrale/thermal sector. Flat, shallow water.
Tramontana works. Northerly wind pushes water south, so some areas get shallower.
Listed as working by spot guides. Onshore at east-shore launches.
Listed as working by spot guides.
Works. Southerly wind raises the water level slightly.
Scirocco, warm and gusty, can go over 30 kn (big-air days). Mostly in spring and autumn.
Not documented by sources. Estimated from beach orientation: offshore at the east-shore launches (Birgi and Contrada Spagnola schools). Confirm locally.

Lo Stagnone, Marsala, Sicily, Italy.launch_notes: Launch from the school/kite-centre areas on the east shore (Birgi and Contrada Spagnola, e.g. Kite Club Marsala, Pro Kite, the 'Kiter Wiese' at Santa Maria in the north). Firm sand or grass rigging areas, knee- to waist-deep water. A kite pass from the centres is usually needed. Advanced riders ride further out and leave the inner zone to students.
Lo Stagnone, Marsala, Sicily, Italy.tide_notes: Practically no tide. Water level depends on wind: northerlies push water south (shallower spots), southerlies raise it slightly. Usually max about 1 m, often under 50 cm.
Lo Stagnone, Marsala, Sicily, Italy.hazards: Very shallow water (often under 50 cm): be careful with jumps and falls. Muddy, silty bottom with seagrass, reeds, rocks and shells that can cut: wear booties. Occasional jellyfish. Gusty Scirocco. Crowded in summer, with many schools and students.
Lo Stagnone, Marsala, Sicily, Italy.rules: Nature reserve (since 1984) and Natura 2000 SIC/ZPS. Kiting is regulated by Capitaneria di Porto Marsala ordinances (zones and entry/exit corridors). Ride beyond 300 m from shore, 200 m inside the reserve. Helmet, buoyancy vest and line cutter required. Hydrofoils banned. Minimum age 14. Legal status contested since 2024 (Legambiente says kiting conflicts with the reserve rules).
Lo Stagnone, Marsala, Sicily, Italy.season: High season June-September (daily thermal wind). Mid season April-May and October (often stronger wind). Kiting possible March-November.

Porto Pollo, Sardinia, Italy.name: Porto Pollo

wind.note: Ponente, the main summer wind. A jet effect through the Strait of Bonifacio speeds it up; usually 15-30 kn (4-8 Bft). Cross to cross-onshore from the left in the west (kite) bay. The bay downwind of the isthmus stays flat.
Reference sector between Ponente and Mistral. You get bump & jump on the windward side of the isthmus and flat water on the lee side.
Mistral. Can go over 30 kn, with gusts to around 40 kn, and can build waves up to about 2 m. For experienced riders.
Tramontana. Often weaker, around 10 kn on average according to the regional tourist board.
Levante is listed as a working wind, using the bay on the other side of the isthmus. Not confirmed for the west kite bay, where it may blow side-off or offshore. Check locally.
Inferred, not stated by any source: the spot is on the north coast, so a south wind blows off the mainland (offshore).

Porto Pollo, Sardinia, Italy.launch_notes: Sandy beaches on both sides of the narrow sand isthmus that joins Isola dei Gabbiani to the mainland. Kite zone: the west bay, on the left side of the peninsula, about 10 min walk from the windsurf centres. It has a big open launch beach and a mobile kite centre. Windsurf zone: the other bay, with direct launch from the centres (Sporting Club Sardinia, MB-Pro Center). Several car parks near the isthmus. Kites and windsurfers use separate zones, so stay in yours.
Porto Pollo, Sardinia, Italy.tide_notes: Very small Mediterranean tide. The kite beach is described as mainly unaffected by tides.
Porto Pollo, Sardinia, Italy.hazards: Very crowded in the summer holidays. The isthmus splits the area, so it divides the two zones. Strong Mistral days bring chop and waves up to about 2 m in the windward bay. Shore break is none to slight. Swimmers are in marked zones.
Porto Pollo, Sardinia, Italy.rules: Kitesurfing and windsurfing have separate zones. Kiting and windsurfing are not allowed in the marked swimming areas of both bays. No specific municipal ordinance (Comune di Palau) was found online, so check with the local centres.
Porto Pollo, Sardinia, Italy.season: April to October/November. The most planing days are in April-May and October-November; June-September is peak season with reliable thermally boosted Ponente. Water is around 16°C in April (4/5 mm wetsuit).

Prasonisi, Rhodes, Greece.name: Prasonisi

wind.note: Meltemi, sped up by a local venturi. Typically 15-30 kn in summer. Onshore on the west (wave) side, strong cross/side-offshore on the east (flat) side.
Onshore to cross-onshore on the west wave beach. The east side stays flat.
Meltemi variant. Cross-onshore on the west beach.
Meltemi from the north. Side-shore on the west beach, offshore on the east beach.
Onshore on the west wave beach.
Offshore on the west wave beach. The next stop downwind is open sea.
Offshore on the west wave beach.

Prasonisi, Rhodes, Greece.launch_notes: Sand tombolo with two back-to-back bays. Kiters mainly use the west wave/onshore beach. Windsurf and wing schools (e.g. Procenter, Prasonisi Windsurf Centre) work on the east flat-water beach in cross-offshore wind. A shallow, standable strip about 20 m wide runs along the sandbar. In July-August the east side is crowded with windsurf students in the afternoons, so keep clear of the teaching area.
Prasonisi, Rhodes, Greece.tide_notes: Tide range is negligible in this part of the Mediterranean. The level changes with the seasons: in winter the water covers the sandbar, in summer the sand strip is exposed.
Prasonisi, Rhodes, Greece.hazards: East side: very strong offshore wind downwind of the spot, with drift out to open sea. West side: steep, punchy waves of 1-2 m or more over the sandbar, with moderate shorebreak. Coral heads reported in the launch area. Shallow channel between the two beaches. Fast windsurfers close to shore. The centres run a rescue boat and a manned watchtower during opening hours.
Prasonisi, Rhodes, Greece.season: May to mid-October. Best June-September; strongest and most consistent in July-August (Meltemi). Facilities close outside roughly April-October.

Vassiliki, Lefkada, Greece.name: Vassiliki

wind.note: Afternoon thermal 'Eric': cross-shore from the right (starboard tack out). Usually 15-20 kn and F5-6, with F7 and 25-30 kn days not unusual. Clouds over the western mountains signal that it is coming.
The NW gradient wind boosts Eric. It comes over the spit on the west side of the bay, so expect gusts.
Gusts strongly down over the long spit that closes the bay to the west. Side-off and gusty near Ponti.
Gentle onshore sea breeze (F1-2) from about 10:00. Good for beginners and light-wind freestyle on the shallow sandbar.
Offshore: the beach faces south, so north wind blows out to sea.

Vassiliki, Lefkada, Greece.launch_notes: The pebble beach at the north of the bay, between Vassiliki village (east) and Ponti (west), is lined with windsurf centres. It is waist-deep with a sand bottom and a sandbar about 50 m out, which is good for beach starts. Launch from the centres' sections. The bay is very busy in season, with 100+ sailors at once.
Vassiliki, Lefkada, Greece.tide_notes: Tidal range is negligible, so the tide does not matter. Sources report no tide and no hidden obstacles under the surface.
Vassiliki, Lefkada, Greece.hazards: Crowded water in season. Strong gusts off the western spit in NW wind. The wind can drop completely in the evening, leaving sailors stranded and needing rescue. Yachts anchor off Ponti. Ferries to Kefalonia/Ithaca use Vassiliki harbour on the east side in summer.
Vassiliki, Lefkada, Greece.rules: Kitesurfing is banned in Vassiliki all year. The nearest kite spot on Lefkada is Agios Ioannis (Milos beach) in the north.
Vassiliki, Lefkada, Greece.season: Late May to October. June, July and August are the most consistent for Eric. May and September are quieter with less wind.

Brouwersdam, Netherlands.name: Brouwersdam

wind.note: Listed as ideal by local school KBC; side-shore along the dam.
Reference direction with W/NW, from Atlantic lows over the British Isles.
Side-on to onshore; choppy North Sea conditions.
Onshore; stronger wind = more chop. Waves mainly at high tide in stormy W-NW.
Onshore; most common strong-wind direction after low pressure moves east.
Onshore; offshore sandbars about 5 km out limit swell to about 1 m.
Side-on.
Listed as working by Windfinder and KBC; side-shore along the dam.
Listed as ideal by KBC; nearly parallel to the shore.
Offshore on the North Sea side. Schools move to the Grevelingen side (Bruinisse) instead.
Offshore on the North Sea side. Schools move to the Grevelingen side (Bruinisse) instead.
Offshore on the North Sea side. Schools move to the Grevelingen side (Bruinisse) instead.

Brouwersdam, Netherlands.launch_notes: Main launch is on the North Sea beach around the middle of the 6.5 km dam. The kite zone, marked by yellow buoys, runs south to the beach pavilion De Kous. The beach at the north end, near the parking by the water, is for windsurfing only. A bay past the slipway at the north end of the dam is tolerated for kiting but not officially allowed. Free parking, large rigging space, shallow shoreline.
Brouwersdam, Netherlands.tide_notes: Low tide gives flat water and standing depth in the shallows, good for learning. High tide brings small waves and a stronger current. Waves only build at high tide in stormy W to NW wind.
Brouwersdam, Netherlands.hazards: Chop builds with onshore wind. Stronger current at high tide. Very busy on windy weekends, with schools, windsurfers and beach users. Respect the buoyed zones and swimmers.
Brouwersdam, Netherlands.rules: Kitesurfing is only allowed in the signposted kite zone on the North Sea side of the dam, marked by yellow buoys up to pavilion De Kous. A 2013 Goeree-Overflakkee decree banned kiting along the coast apart from this Brouwersdam strip; it expired in July 2023. Check the current local signs.
Brouwersdam, Netherlands.season: Apr-May and Sep-Oct are best; usable all year. Schools operate roughly late March to early November.

Wijk aan Zee, Netherlands.name: Wijk aan Zee

wind.note: Cross-shore. Gives the biggest waves at the spot.
Gives the cleanest waves, which wrap around the 400 m harbour wall. Needs more wind, and the pier may block some of it.
Onshore to cross-onshore. Expect choppy conditions.
The most common wind direction here. The beach also takes swell from SW to N.
Windfinder lists the De HangOut kitespot as working in northerly winds.
Offshore. KNRM has rescued kiters here after the wind suddenly turned offshore.
Offshore.

Wijk aan Zee, Netherlands.launch_notes: Launch from the beach north of the Noordpier, near the beach bars and surf schools. The car park is behind the dunes, so expect a long walk to the beach. Guides mention two more launches further north along the coast. Local schools include Kiteflow and Ozlines. The spot is often crowded with windsurfers and kitesurfers, so keep your distance.
Wijk aan Zee, Netherlands.tide_notes: Waves depend heavily on the tide and can build sharply at high water. Plan your session around the tide.
Wijk aan Zee, Netherlands.hazards: Rip currents close to the jetty. Crowded with windsurfers, kiters and surfers. A sudden turn to offshore wind has led to KNRM rescues. Water pollution has been reported near the industrial harbour and steel works. Theft from cars has been reported.
Wijk aan Zee, Netherlands.season: Rideable all year. Waves are usually smaller in summer.

Fehmarn Gold, Germany.name: Fehmarn Gold

wind.note: Reference direction. Flat to small chop, short and steep, waves rarely above 0.5 m. Large shallow area where you can stand.
Reference direction. Works well in south to west winds.
Best direction according to surf-magazin. The headland 2 km upwind blocks the bigger waves in W to NW winds.
Usable. The headland upwind keeps the water fairly flat.
Usable. The headland upwind keeps the water fairly flat.
surf-magazin gives south to west to NNW as the working range.
Works. You can sail across to the opposite peninsula, but the water in between is too deep to stand.

surf-magazin says easterly winds do not work (offshore here). One kite blog says Gold works in E, so check locally.

Fehmarn Gold, Germany.launch_notes: Big parking area about 100 m from the water. You get to the water over a grass meadow. Kiters usually launch further right, windsurfers increasingly on the left. Kiters have their own zone. Watch out for the groyne to the left of the entrance (it is visible). Tim's Beach (school and rental), toilets and Café Achterndiek are on site.
Fehmarn Gold, Germany.tide_notes: No real tide (Baltic). The water is less than 1.5 m deep over a large area, so wind-driven water level changes affect how deep it is.
Fehmarn Gold, Germany.hazards: Rocky dike and groyne areas, plus a groyne next to the entrance. Shallow water with seagrass. Very crowded in summer, so collisions are a risk. Water gets too deep to stand between Gold and the opposite peninsula.
Fehmarn Gold, Germany.rules: Separate kite zone. Follow right-of-way rules and sail with foresight, especially with summer crowds. Parking fee in summer.

St. Peter-Ording, Germany.name: St. Peter-Ording

wind.note: Works at Südstrand and Böhl lagoon areas.
Side-on; usable on all beaches.
Cross-onshore. Best for the wave in front of Ording. SW storms bring the best wave riding. Ideal for the Südstrand lagoon.

Onshore to cross-onshore. Good at the main beach and Südstrand.
Cross-onshore; good at all beaches.
Very good at Ording/FKK beach and Böhl, especially in the last two hours of the rising tide.
Side-shore; works at the main beach (SW to N range).
Side-off. Guides list Südstrand/Böhl as working from SE, but use caution.
Offshore. Kiters should never go out in offshore wind. Windsurfers sometimes ride it because the beach is so wide, but there is a drift risk.

St. Peter-Ording, Germany.launch_notes: Main area is Ordinger Strand, reached by car over a dike crossing. You can park and rig directly on the beach (parking fee). Kite zones lie left and right of the swimming area in front of the beach car park, marked with white/yellow buoys. Kiting in the swim zone is banned. Areas are shared with windsurfers: keep your distance and keep launch zones clear. Böhler Strand (south) is best for beginners: wide standing area, less traffic, but a longer walk.
St. Peter-Ording, Germany.tide_notes: Very tide-dependent. Shallow tideways form at low tide (good for beginners). Higher water brings waves on the outer sandbanks. Südstrand lagoon and Böhl only work about 2 h before to 2 h after high tide; at low water the sea runs out too far to ride. Distance from parking to the water can reach about 500 m. Storm surges can flood the beach car park.
St. Peter-Ording, Germany.hazards: Strong tidal current: runs north on the rising tide and south on the falling tide. Drift risk rises when wind and current line up. Reaching the outer sandbanks takes experience and fitness. The wave off Ording breaks unpredictably. Little real shorebreak thanks to the sandbanks. Can get crowded at the main beach at peak times.
St. Peter-Ording, Germany.rules: Kitesurfing only inside the buoyed kite zones on either side of the swimming area. Kiting in the bathing zone is prohibited. Overnight camping and BBQs on the beach are prohibited. The beach lies at the edge of the Schleswig-Holstein Wadden Sea National Park.
St. Peter-Ording, Germany.season: Late March to early June and September to November. Windiest months: March, April, June, September, October, November. Year-round when not frozen.

Sylt Westerland, Germany.name: Sylt Westerland (Brandenburger Strand)

wind.note: Sideshore along the west coast; at 20 kn and more it is a fun wave session (surf-magazin).
Sideshore, cited with N as a reference direction for 20 kn+ sessions.
Open North Sea; onshore leaning, so conditions are challenging with big shorebreak.
Straight onshore, typically 15-35 kn; rough, demanding conditions for experienced riders only.
Sideshore from S-SW at 20 kn+ gives good wave riding.
Sideshore, cited with SW as a reference direction.
Fully offshore at Westerland.

Sylt Westerland, Germany.launch_notes: Launch and land on Brandenburger Strand, the main beach in front of the Westerland promenade (GKA Kite World Cup and Windsurf World Cup venue). Keep clear of swimming zones and of the groynes on the west side. Check the information boards on the beach for current zones. Parking behind the dike gets crowded in summer.
Sylt Westerland, Germany.tide_notes: Runs cleanest around low tide: shorebreak and wave height near the shore stay moderate, and small flat-water pools form in places. As the tide rises the sets reach the shore and the shorebreak can get extreme at high tide. Tidal range is larger in westerly winds and at spring tides.
Sylt Westerland, Germany.hazards: Powerful, mast-breaking shorebreak; short standing area; noticeable current across the whole area; stone groynes in the water (the remaining one is marked with yellow crosses). Wear a helmet and impact vest. Crowded in summer.
Sylt Westerland, Germany.rules: Inside the Schleswig-Holstein Wadden Sea National Park area. Seasonal bathing zones: with a green or yellow flag, windsurfing is restricted in the guarded bathing areas; with a red flag, water access is unrestricted. Stay out of swimming zones and away from groynes. Follow the zoning shown on beach signs.
Sylt Westerland, Germany.season: Apr-Jun and Sep-Oct are best; windiest Oct-Mar.

Hvide Sande, Denmark.name: Hvide Sande

wind.note: The reference wind per guides: westerlies with some north in them. Blows side-off/offshore over the dune strip, so it is gusty near shore and steadier further out. Shallow water reaches ~800 m out, and in an emergency you drift across to the fjord's far shore.
Westerlies with a northerly component work best. Gusty near shore. Choppy wind waves build further out in strong wind.
Usable on the fjord. Strong NW–N is also the wave-riding direction on the North Sea side at the south mole, for experts only.
Works, but the Hvide Sande Syd spot (55.9854, 8.1385) is rated better in SW.
Onshore. The local guide (Westwind) lists onshore winds as a hazard.

Hvide Sande, Denmark.launch_notes: Fjord-side spot north of Hvide Sande, signposted for windsurfing. Large paid car park a few metres from a grass rigging area and a small sandy beach. Facilities: Westwind centre (school, rental, shop, showers, toilets, storage boxes). Busy with windsurfers, and kiters are asked to keep out of their way.
Hvide Sande, Denmark.tide_notes: The fjord is brackish and shallow, fed with seawater through the Hvide Sande sluice/harbour opening. It is mostly standing to chest depth. Ringkøbing Fjord is not really tidal.
Hvide Sande, Denmark.hazards: Fishing nets and net poles. Bathers, dogs and children near shore. Short, unpleasant chop further out in strong wind. Gusts near shore in westerlies. At Hvide Sande Syd it gets very shallow near shore (risk of grounding, fin strikes). North Sea side: strong currents, always running outward along both harbour piers, can be life-threatening.
Hvide Sande, Denmark.rules: No formal kite zones are listed for Hvide Sande Nord. Windsurfing and kitesurfing are banned at the 'Betweens' spot between the harbour moles on the North Sea side.
Hvide Sande, Denmark.season: April–November. March–May and September–November are the windiest; summer winds are lighter. You always need a wetsuit.

Camber Sands, England.name: Camber Sands (Broomhill)

wind.note: Prevailing direction, cross-onshore from the right looking out to sea.
Cross-onshore; works well.

Cross-shore; usable, quoted as the western limit of the working range.

Onshore, usable.
Listed as a working direction.
Eastern limit of the working range; for easterlies the council points riders to Greatstone instead.
Offshore. Council: 'Do not use this area' in northwesterlies.

Camber Sands, England.launch_notes: Launch in the designated Water Sports Zone in front of Broomhill Sands car park (free parking, Lydd Road, home of The Kitesurf Centre). Teaching zone runs from the black/white flag west to the first houses; freeride zone runs from the flag east to the MOD range. Kiting is banned at the Dunes end of Camber. Launch at least 50m (local guide: 75m) from people and hard hazards, ideally at the water's edge.
Camber Sands, England.tide_notes: Very tidal (spring range around 8m). No kiting from 2.5–3 hours before to 2.5–3 hours after high tide, because the water reaches the sea defence wall and there is no launch area left. Flat tidal pools form on the rising and falling tide. Shore break and strong currents at high tide.
Camber Sands, England.hazards: Sea defence wall and steps, granite rock boulders, wooden groynes, two shipwrecks at the east end (visible at low tide), MOD live firing range to the east, shore break and strong currents around high tide.
Camber Sands, England.rules: Only fly inside the designated kite zones, and keep to the separate teaching and freeride zones. Third-party insurance is required. No kiting at the Dunes end. Do not ride or enter the water in front of the MOD range when red flags are flying. No riding around high tide (council: 3 h either side). Water sports are not advised in offshore winds.
Camber Sands, England.season: Main riding season is March to November, busiest June to September (SW winds plus afternoon summer sea breezes). The windiest months are October to April.

Hunstanton, England.name: Hunstanton

Hunstanton, England.launch_notes: Main beach in front of the town (New Hunstanton) at low tide. Old Hunstanton at mid to high tide: north of the resort, no sea wall, car park, toilets and café on site. Kite Eze (IKO school) teaches at Old Hunstanton, PE36 6JL. Sand bars and shallow flat water make it a good place to learn.
Hunstanton, England.tide_notes: Can be sailed at all tides; medium tidal range. Low tide: flat lagoon behind the sandbar, good for freestyle but shallow. Mid tide: shallow and choppier. High tide on the main beach: water against the 4 m sea defences between wooden groynes, dangerous for kiters. Go to Old Hunstanton at high tide. The flood comes in fast over the sandbanks and can cut people off.
Hunstanton, England.hazards: 4 m sea wall and old wooden groynes at high tide on the main beach. Sandbars and very shallow water at low tide. Fast incoming tide can strand people on the sandbanks. Strong unpredictable gusts: a kiter was lifted about 20 ft and seriously injured at Old Hunstanton. No lifeguards at Old Hunstanton.

Rhosneigr, Wales.name: Rhosneigr

Ideal for sideshore wave riding.
Prevailing wind, which speeds up between Wales and Ireland. Sideshore to cross-onshore wave conditions.

Inside the SW–NW range that guides list as rideable.
Guides say NW can give very good wave conditions.
Windsurf guides call N a good wave direction, but it runs side to side-off on a beach facing WSW. Check on site.

Offshore. Blows over the village, so it is very gusty and full of holes.

Rhosneigr, Wales.launch_notes: Kitesurfers mostly use Traeth Crigyll, the northern town beach, and launch along Glan-y-Môr Road. At high tide there is a wind shadow near Glan-y-Môr Road, so launch further south near Funsport. Launch and ride well away from the rocks that split the two beaches. Surfers mostly use Traeth Llydan (Broad Beach) to the south. Parking on Glan-y-Môr Road and Beach Road fills early; park around the edges of the grass areas.
Rhosneigr, Wales.tide_notes: Rideable at all tides. Mid-tide is best: clean kickers and swell, plus room to rig. At high tide the beach is narrow and rigging space gets tight. From mid to low tide rocks are exposed, and windsurf guides warn of submerged rocks near high water. The best waves come on the incoming tide.
Rhosneigr, Wales.hazards: Strong rip and submerged rocks at the southern end of the bay. Rocks between Traeth Crigyll and Traeth Llydan. The river that cuts across the beach halfway up (near the dunes) has a strong rip after heavy rain. Wind shadow at high tide near Glan-y-Môr Road. Keep clear of sailing lanes marked by yellow buoys. Can get crowded on good days.
Rhosneigr, Wales.rules: Anglesey Council seashore byelaws set an 8-knot speed limit for craft. Traeth Llydan is a launch site where launching fees apply to powered craft. No overnight van parking on Glan-y-Môr Road; campervans and motorhomes are restricted from 12:00 to 08:00.
Rhosneigr, Wales.season: Windy all year. Spring and summer are milder. Best sessions come with S–SW wind and swell.

Dakhla lagoon, Morocco.name: Dakhla lagoon

wind.note: Prevailing trade wind, side-shore over the lagoon. Usually 15-25 kn, stronger Apr-Sep (up to 35 kn), often lighter in the morning and picking up in the early afternoon.
Prevailing trade wind, side-shore along the lagoon. Funnelled and gusty near the dunes.
Part of the trade wind sector, side to side-on.
Rare (about 1-2 times a year, per IKSURFMAG).

Dakhla lagoon, Morocco.launch_notes: Launch from the kite camps on the western shore of the lagoon (Dakhla Attitude on its point, PK25, Westpoint, Lagoon Village...), about 25-30 min from town. Each camp has its own beach, school, rental and rescue. If you ride without staying at a camp, get a rescue voucher. Speed Spot (east shore, about 23.87895,-15.74894) is reached by 4x4/boat or by riding across; little or no assistance there.
Dakhla lagoon, Morocco.tide_notes: Rideable at all tides. Low tide: flat, standing-depth water for about 300 m from the beach; expect a carry of up to about 350 m, and some areas get very shallow. High tide: deeper water and chop, especially in strong wind. Tides are bigger at full and new moon. Speed Spot only works around low tide, when a sandbank of about 600 m forms across the wind.
Dakhla lagoon, Morocco.hazards: Gusty wind, worse near the dunes and around full moon. Chop at high tide. Very shallow areas and exposed sandbanks at low tide. Sharp shell fragments on the beach (boots recommended). Busy in peak summer. Strong current in the channel inside Dragon Island if riding to Speed Spot. Remote site with limited rescue outside the camps.
Dakhla lagoon, Morocco.rules: No specific kite rules reported (common sense). Part of Dakhla Bay is a Ramsar wetland and an Important Bird Area (ZICO); oyster farms sit on the lagoon edges.
Dakhla lagoon, Morocco.season: Year-round (about 300-340 windy days a year). Strongest Apr-Sep, peak Jun-Aug. Nov-Apr has lighter wind, good for beginners. Weakest in Dec-Jan.

Essaouira, Morocco.name: Essaouira Bay

wind.note: Main summer trade wind (Alizé/Charki) direction, made stronger by the afternoon thermal. 20-30+ kn in Jul-Aug, side to side-onshore along the 5 km arc.
Trade-wind variant. Guides call it cross to cross-onshore. Often stronger in the afternoon.
Side-onshore. Gusty near the medina because the town wind shadow disturbs it.
Wannakitesurf lists NW side-onshore as a reference direction. Very gusty close to the city because buildings disturb the flow.
Guides list NE as the trade direction, but given the beach orientation it is likely side-off, especially in the mornings. Check on site.
Mostly winter. Less predictable and sometimes slightly cross-offshore in the morning before it turns onshore.
Winter secondary wind. Less reliable than the summer trades.

Essaouira, Morocco.launch_notes: Launch from the long, wide sandy beach south of the medina walls, in front of the schools and rental centres in the middle and downwind part of the bay. Rig away from horse and camel tours, tourists and locals. Stay out of the swimming zones. Do not launch near the town at the north end, where wind is gusty and rocks are hidden.
Essaouira, Morocco.tide_notes: Works at all tides on a sandy bottom, but guides rate high tide best. At high tide the small river-mouth lagoon at the south end of the bay fills with flat, glassy water for freestyle, with room for only a few riders.
Essaouira, Morocco.hazards: Hidden rocks and very gusty wind near the town and harbour (north/right side). Launching and landing are dangerous on strong days because of gusts. The beach is crowded with horse and camel tours, swimmers and other watercraft, especially at weekends. Mogador island shelters the bay from swell. Waves get bigger to the south, where the island stops blocking them, and in spring/autumn reach 1-2 m. Current is weak (<1 kn).
Essaouira, Morocco.season: Rideable all year. Most reliable from April to September, with a peak in July-August (about 90% windy days, often 25-30+ kn). Main season runs May to October.

Cumbuco, Ceará, Brazil.name: Cumbuco

wind.note: Trade wind with thermal boost from the dunes, often stronger in the afternoon. Cross-onshore from the right.
Average direction of the SE trades. Cross to cross-onshore from the right, usually 15-25 kn from Aug to Dec.
Usual morning direction, side to side-offshore, before it turns side-onshore in the afternoon. Be careful when it is gusty near shore.
Side-offshore. Guides say to move to other spots north or south of Cumbuco when it goes offshore.
Offshore at the main beach.

Cumbuco, Ceará, Brazil.launch_notes: Main kite zone is on the beach in front of the Eco Paradise hotel, where most kiters gather. The beach is wide, so you can move about 150 m up or downwind to find space. It gets busier with obstacles near the village center. The usual downwinder goes to Lagoa do Cauipe (about 6 km downwind) for flat water.
Cumbuco, Ceará, Brazil.tide_notes: Main beach is described as not tide dependent. Sandbanks further out make small waves. The size of the Cauipe lagoon depends on water level (rainy season), not on the tide.
Cumbuco, Ceará, Brazil.hazards: Chop and small shorebreak, sandbanks offshore. Current of 1-2 kn. Swimmers and other boats in the water. Crowded on weekends and in peak season, especially at Cauipe lagoon. Theft of gear and valuables reported.
Cumbuco, Ceará, Brazil.season: June to February. Best from August to December, kiteable almost every day (10-14 m kites). Little wind from March to May (rainy season).

Jericoacoara, Brazil.name: Jericoacoara (Preá)

wind.note: Reference trade wind, cross-shore from the right along the Preá–Jericoacoara strip. Typically 16–35 kn in season, blowing until sunset.
Frequent trade direction, cross to slightly cross-offshore from the right. Listed as a working direction by spot guides.
Cross-onshore, usable along the beach strip.
Cross-onshore, usable.
Listed as a working direction (thekitespot). Close to onshore.
Side-offshore at the beach. Listed by windy.app, but it gets gusty and drifts riders out to sea.
Offshore.
Offshore.

Jericoacoara, Brazil.launch_notes: The main kite launch is on the wide, flat sandy beach at Preá, home to most schools and kite centers. You can kite anywhere along the 14 km strip from Barrinha to Preá. Preá→Jeri is a short downwinder. The landing near the Jeri sunset dune is not for beginners, and wind in front of Jeri is gusty. Flat-water lagoons downwind: Guriú (medium to high tide), Tatajuba, and Barra Grande (low tide).
Jericoacoara, Brazil.tide_notes: The ocean beach works at all tides. Low tide gives shallower, flat-to-choppy water. Rising and high tide bring kickers and small waves. The lagoons depend on the tide: Guriú works at medium–high tide, Barra Grande is best at low tide, and Tatajuba changes size with the tide. Check depth before trying tricks.
Jericoacoara, Brazil.hazards: Sand buggies and 4x4s drive along the beach and may not see lines or gear. Medium alongshore current (1–2 kn). Near Jericoacoara village: boats, rocks and buildings close to the beach, and gusty wind off the dune. Very crowded in peak season.
Jericoacoara, Brazil.rules: The beach is in Jericoacoara National Park (ICMBio). Kiting and kite landing are banned on Jeri's main beach, which is reserved for windsurfers. A kite zone lies past the sunset dune, and windsurfing is banned within 500 m of shore in that zone. Kite/windsurf schools need a 12-month park authorization (ICMBio portaria, 2016).
Jericoacoara, Brazil.season: July to January (peak August–January, 20–38 kn). February is mid-season. Lighter winds March–June.

Barra Grande, Piauí, Brazil.name: Barra Grande

wind.note: Steady trade wind, typically 18-24 kn (range 15-35 kn), side-shore to side-on from the right (starboard). Stronger in the afternoon.
Side-on starboard, the reference direction in the season.
Side-shore. Usable trade-wind variant.
More onshore. Choppier, harder to get upwind of the shallows.
Some guides call SE the main direction, but on this north-facing coast it turns side-off and gusty. Check on site.
Offshore.
Offshore.

Barra Grande, Piauí, Brazil.launch_notes: Wide sandy beach about 4-5 km long in front of the village (Cajueiro da Praia municipality), with several kite schools and pousadas along it. Launch from the beach in front of the schools. Give learners room in the shallows. Downwinders run to nearby lagoons (Barrinha, Mangue) and further on to the river mouth area (Macapá).
Barra Grande, Piauí, Brazil.tide_notes: Very tide-dependent. Mid to low tide gives flat, waist-deep water, and lagoons/pools form on the sea side: ideal for beginners and freestyle. Right at low tide some areas get too shallow. High tide makes the water deeper and choppy, with small waves on the outer sandbank.
Barra Grande, Piauí, Brazil.hazards: Shallow sandbanks: jumping or falling in very shallow water near the edges risks injury. Shore break of about 2 m over the outer sandbank at higher tides. Sandy bottom, little current reported. Spot guides mention visible hazards without saying what they are.
Barra Grande, Piauí, Brazil.season: July to January (most consistent August to December, peak in August-September)
